title: A double bond takes hydrogen
hook: Predict the product, then compare the bonds.

knows: Structural formula bonds and common organic functional groups.
doesNotKnow: Hydrogenation adds a hydrogen to each carbon of the double bond. The two carbons remain connected, while C=C becomes C–C and the organic product is ethane.

misconception: Reaction conditions do not affect the connectivity of the product.
objective: Predict the organic product of ethene under the stated conditions and identify the changed connectivity.

claims.text: Question, structural diagrams, product and explanation: Ethene is treated with H₂ and a palladium catalyst. Which major organic product forms after workup? Hydrogenation adds a hydrogen to each carbon of the double bond. The two carbons remain connected, while C=C becomes C–C and the organic product is ethane.
The diagrams use condensed labels and depict connectivity rather than molecular geometry; highlighting identifies selected changed groups.
